Counterproductive

/kown-ter-pruh-DUK-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Counterproductive means having the opposite of the intended, useful effect; backfiring instead of helping.

Counterproductive means having the opposite of the intended, useful effect; backfiring instead of helping. Padlocking the suggestion box proved counterproductive: complaints doubled once employees felt silenced.

Worked Example

After a losing streak, a basketball coach began punishing every defeat with extra two-hour drills late into the night. The players grew so exhausted that their shooting got worse, their tempers got shorter, and the team dropped even more games. A plan meant to build winners was actually manufacturing losses. The assistant coach finally said aloud what everyone suspected: the punishment drills were counterproductive.

The extra drills were meant to improve the team but produced the opposite effect, more losses, which is exactly what counterproductive describes.

How Counterproductive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

self-defeating

self-defeating: working against one's own goal

self-sabotaging

self-sabotaging: undermining one's own effort or plan

Antonyms

effective

effective: producing the intended result

beneficial

beneficial: producing good, helpful effects

How Strong Is It? — unproductive → counterproductive → ruinous

unproductive vs. counterproductive

unproductive vs. counterproductive: An unproductive effort simply fails to accomplish anything, while a counterproductive one actively pushes the goal further away.

ruinous vs. counterproductive

ruinous vs. counterproductive: Counterproductive actions set back the goal they were meant to serve, but ruinous actions destroy the whole enterprise beyond repair.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — counter-

Prefix — counter-: against, in opposition to, from Latin contra

Root — product

Root — product: from Latin producere, to bring forth, from pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead'

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality of, tending to

Put it together

Put it together: Counterproductive joins counter-, 'against,' to productive, from Latin producere, 'to bring forth' (pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead'). Something counterproductive literally leads against the very result you were trying to bring forth.

Use the root in a new word: deduce

Use the root in a new word: deduce: From the muddy boots by the door, she could deduce that her brother had taken the trail home, literally leading her reasoning down from the evidence, as the root ducere suggests.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, everyday and academic register

Counterproductive describes actions, policies, or strategies, not people, and it always implies active backfiring. If an effort merely accomplishes nothing, call it unproductive; reserve counterproductive for efforts that make the problem worse than before.
